definition: Model-agnostic attribution methods assigning each input feature a contribution to a specific prediction (SHAP with game-theoretic guarantees, LIME via local surrogate models).
details: Model-agnostic attribution methods assigning each input feature a contribution to a specific prediction (SHAP with game-theoretic guarantees, LIME via local surrogate models). The workhorses of tabular-model explanation in regulated industries.

explainer.lead: LIME is a model-agnostic attribution method that assigns each input feature a contribution to a specific prediction using local surrogate models. It matters as a workhorse for explaining tabular models in regulated industries.

tiers.eli5: It's like asking 'why did the model say this?' by building a simple, easy-to-understand model around that one prediction to see which inputs mattered most.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use LIME to generate local explanations for individual predictions by fitting an interpretable surrogate model around the instance; a pitfall is that the explanations can be unstable, so results should be checked with multiple samples.
tiers.paperLevel: LIME is a model-agnostic attribution method that assigns each input feature a contribution to a specific prediction via local surrogate models; unlike SHAP, it lacks game-theoretic guarantees, which is a known limitation.

explainer.example: For a loan rejection, LIME might show that income and credit score contributed most to the denial, by fitting a sparse linear model around that applicant's data.
